newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Singapore said keen on Philippine port project.
newsitem.headline: Singapore said keen on Philippine port project.

text.p: Singapore had expressed interest to invest in the development of a better port in Bacolod City in the central Philippines in partnership with Filipino investors, a senior Bacolod businessman said on Monday.

Bacolod Chamber of Commerce and Industry chairman Roberto Montelibano told reporters in an interview officials of state-agency Port of Singapore Authority had expressed interest to team up with local businessmen for the development of a new port or the expansion of the government-owned Pulupandan port in the area.
Bacolod is the centre of the Philippine sugar trade.
"We have 800,000 tonnes of sugar to move (annually) but because we don't have (enough) port facilities, the transport of sugar takes longer time and entails additional costs," Montelibano said.
Sugar farmers said a new port has to be built in Bacolod to speed up transport of the commodity. They said facilities at the Pulupandan and the private-owned Banago port were not enough.
